name: Periyar Tiger Reserve (Thekkady)
tagline: Lakeside wildlife reserve and spice‑hill gateway in the Western Ghats
summary: Periyar Tiger Reserve at Thekkady is Kerala’s best‑known wildlife sanctuary — boat cruises, guided walks and community ecotourism bring jungle, elephants and birdlife close to visitors.
description: Periyar Tiger Reserve (often called Periyar or Thekkady) is a protected area in the Cardamom and Western Ghats ranges of Idukki district. The park centres on the Periyar Lake — an impounded reservoir — and protects evergreen and moist deciduous forest, elephants, tigers, primates and rich birdlife.

Thekkady is the main visitor town and gateway: most tourists take the early morning or late afternoon boat cruises on Periyar Lake for reliable wildlife viewing. The reserve also runs guided nature walks, bamboo rafting, watch‑towers and longer treks organized by the forest department and partner organisations.

Periyar matters for conservation (it is a tiger and elephant reserve) and for local livelihoods: many ecotourism programmes employ tribal and local communities and proceeds support reserve management and local welfare.

A visit gives close wildlife viewing from the lake, short guided treks, spice‑garden visits near Kumily and easy access to nearby attractions such as Mangaladevi temple, cardamom hills and KTDC heritage properties.
highlights: Boat safari on Periyar Lake (about 1.5 hours) for elephants, deer and birds
Guided nature walks, bamboo rafting and border/park treks
Community ecotourism programmes and tribal performances
KTDC and forest department lodging options near the lake
Mangaladevi ruins and spice plantation tours from Kumily/Thekkady

sections.heading: Background
body: Periyar Tiger Reserve (also called Periyar Wildlife Sanctuary or Periyar National Park) protects mid‑elevation forests of the southern Western Ghats and was declared a tiger reserve under India’s Project Tiger. The reserve covers core and buffer ranges around the Periyar reservoir and is an elephant reserve as well.
Management combines Kerala Forest & Wildlife Department operations with community ecotourism partners and conservation foundations that run guided programmes and visitor services.

sections.heading: Wildlife and visitor experiences
body: The most common and reliable way to see wildlife is the scheduled boat cruise on Periyar Lake; boats circle feeding zones where elephants, sambar, gaur and many bird species gather. The reserve also offers organized nature walks, watch‑tower visits, bamboo rafting and longer trail programmes that must be booked through the forest department or official operators.

Specialist programmes (Periyar Trail, overnight jungle camps, border hikes and village/community experiences) run on fixed days and usually require advance booking; local operators and the Periyar Tiger Reserve website list current programmes and schedules.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Thekkady/Kumily is the tourism hub. Book boat cruises, walks or specialised treks through the Periyar Tiger Reserve website or the official forest/tourism counters; KTDC and local eco‑operators also sell packages. Arrive early for morning boats (best wildlife activity) and check timing restrictions — some lodges must reach before evening forest checkposts close.
Nearest railhead and airports are not in Thekkady — travellers normally reach Thekkady by road from Kottayam (railhead) or Madurai/Cochin airports and continue by car/bus/taxi to Kumily/Thekkady.

sections.heading: Responsible travel & conservation
body: Follow forest department rules: stay on designated trails and boats, obey guides, keep noise low and do not feed wildlife. Many programmes are community‑run; choosing official operators helps local livelihoods and conservation funding.
Confirm bookings and circulation rules (boat schedules, walk group sizes, check‑post timings) with official reservation channels before travel.

latest.text: Periyar Tiger Reserve official site lists the standard 1.5‑hour boat cruises and program schedules and provides a tourism/boating contact for bookings (see official page).
KTDC notes an entry/checkpost timing rule for guests arriving at KTDC properties (guests should reach before 5 pm because forest checkpost entry closes after that).

Recent checked programme rates list the Periyar Nature Walk at an official programme rate (example listing checked 6 Sep 2026 showed ₹400 per person with a minimum group charge — confirm current rate before travel).

visitorInfo.bestTime: September–March (cooler months and better wildlife visibility; monsoon June–August restricts some activities)
visitorInfo.howToReach: Kumily/Thekkady is best reached by road. Nearest railhead is Kottayam (~114 km) and nearest major airports used are Madurai (~110 km) or Kochi; regular buses, taxis and private cars connect to Kumily/Thekkady. Book boat/walk programmes through the Periyar Tiger Reserve website or forest counters.
etiquette: Book boat cruises and guided walks in advance through the official Periyar reservation channels.
Arrive early for morning boats — wildlife activity is highest then and light is best for photography.
Carry rain protection in shoulder seasons and footwear suitable for short forest walks; always follow guide instructions.
